audit.evidence: app.rb runs the REAL sanitize gem (gem install sanitize -v 5.2.0/5.2.1/6.0.1 + real nokogiri/nokogumbo/crass) via Sinatra/WEBrick; real headless Chromium (selenium/standalone-chromium) victim proves JS execution. Live gate on real Docker: v0 flag, v1 orig (math/svg) blocked, v1 bypass (noscript desync) flag, v2 residual empty (blocked). 4-way closure.

app_purpose: server-side HTML sanitization allowlist: clean untrusted markup with a custom RELAXED+noscript config before displaying it in a page
root_cause: Mutation XSS (mXSS) / sanitizer allowlist bypass via HTML parsing desync: content that Sanitize's Nokogiri/gumbo parser treats as inert text is re-parsed as LIVE markup by a scripting-enabled browser -- first through non-allowlisted <math>/<svg> foreign-content whose contents 5.2.0 failed to strip, then through an allowlisted <noscript> element that Nokogiri parses with SCRIPTING DISABLED while browsers parse it with SCRIPTING ENABLED (CWE-79)

invariant_deps.note: On v0/v1 the whole parse stack (nokogiri 1.13.10 + nokogumbo 2.0.5 providing Nokogiri::HTML5 + crass 1.0.6) is pinned IDENTICAL so the SOLE variable between the vulnerable and the incomplete-fix env is the sanitize gem (5.2.0 vs 5.2.1). Sanitize 6.x REQUIRES nokogiri >= 1.12 (gumbo built in) and drops the nokogumbo dependency, so v2 uses nokogiri 1.13.10's built-in HTML5 parser (no nokogumbo). That parser-backend change is inherent to the 5.x->6.x major bump and cannot be pinned identical; the constant is the Nokogiri libxml2/gumbo *scripting-disabled* parse rule that is the root cause of the desync.

sink.detail_v1_fix: 5.2.1: :remove_contents %w[iframe noembed noframes noscript script style] -> %w[iframe math noembed noframes noscript plaintext script style svg xmp] (adds math/svg/plaintext/xmp) -- CVE-2020-4054
sink.detail_v2_fix: 6.0.1: CleanElement gains `when 'noscript' then node.unlink` so noscript is always removed even when allowlisted -- CVE-2023-23627

poc.allowlist_note: Config = Sanitize's RELAXED config PLUS `noscript` in the element allowlist. RELAXED already allows `style`/`img`/`title` but NOT `math`/`svg`/`noscript`. evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: GHSA-p4x4-rw2p-8j8m named `noscript` among the dangerous elements and was fixed in 5.2.1 by extending :remove_contents; but :remove_contents only strips FILTERED elements, so an allowlisted `noscript` stayed exploitable via the scripting-disabled/enabled parse desync until 6.0.1 unconditionally unlinked it (GHSA-fw3g-2h3j-qmm7). Upstream regression tests: 5.2.1 added the `<math>/<svg>` foreign-content test, 6.0.1 added `<noscript><div id='</noscript><img src=x onerror=alert(1)> '>` under 'sanitization bypass by exploiting scripting-disabled <noscript> behavior'.

Genuine incomplete fix: 5.2.1 stripped the math/svg foreign-content leak but left the sibling noscript scripting-desync of the same sink live until 6.0.1. Confirmed empirically that the noscript residual genuinely EXECUTES in scripting-enabled headless Chromium (not mere reflection).
